newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St lifts London, Frankfurt to new peaks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St lifts London, Frankfurt to new peaks.

text.p: London and Frankfurt stocks roared ahead to new trading peaks on Tuesday, boosted by a blistering overnight rally in New York which drove Wall Street to a record close.

On currency markets the dollar was subdued but sterling bounded forward after Britain raised interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point. The move, coupled with sweeping monetray reforms by the new Labour administration, also gave a big lift to government bonds.

Most of the action was in equity markets. London opened at a record trading high, fell slightly, then roared ahead by 1.5 percent to 4525.6 points on the FTSE index, passing the peak set only an hour earlier.
Frankfurt also hit an intra-day record with a leap of 1.2 percent. Madrid and Brussels too were in bullish mood, reaching new peaks but Paris fell, held back by political uncertainties.

The engine driving the big advances in Europe was New York's performance on Monday where stocks were lifted by hopes that a balanced budget agreement would keep the U.S. central bank from raising interest rates later this month.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 143.29 points, or 2 percent, to 7,214.49, beating the old mark of 7,085.16 set on March 11 and its 16th record so far this year.

"It was almost like a tidal wave coming," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. It was one of the biggest point gains ever for the 30-share average and other market averages also set records.

London stocks, which hesitated on news that a regular monthly monetary meeting had been brought forward, rebounded sharply on relief that new finance minister Gordon Brown had made an early and decisive move to raise interest rates.
"Everyone was expecting a 25 basis point rise and that's what they got," commented Steve Wright, UK equity strategist at BZW.
"The (equity) futures had sold off ahead of this news on worries that the rate rise might be half a point and that would have been seen as overly aggressive," said one futures specialist.

Just two days into the new government the leading FTSE index has responded with record performances, setting an intraday peak of 4,468.4 on Friday, the last trading day because of a public holiday yesterday.
Besides raising rates to 6.25 percent from six percent, the new Labour government gave the central bank greater powers in a radical move that changes the mechanics of setting monetary policy.

"Giving more independence to the Bank of England to set interest rates is probably more significant than the fact that interest rates have gone up," said Wright at BZW. "It is a long way towards an independent central bank, which is a very euro-friendly policy."
Brown brought forward a planned meeting with Bank of England governor Eddie George by 24 hours and told reporters afterwards he was giving the central bank independence to set interest rates.

The economy has been growing at more than three percent and George was concerned about the build-up of inflationary pressures. Brown said the Treasury will continue to set the inflation target, which will remain at 2.5 percent.

In Frankfurt, stocks advanced to 3584.56 points near the opening, beating the previous trading high of 3533.18 set only yesterday amid a batch of positive corporate news reports and New York's strong performance.
The market fell back slightly on profit-taklng but was still showing gains comfortably above one percent by midday.
"All the news has been positive today," said a Frankfurt dealer. "Wall Street was good, the Nikkei was better and we are simply keeping up."
Paris stood out, the only major European bourse to show a loss. French stocks opened higher but quickly fell and were 0.6 percent in the minus column by lunch-time.
French investors were clearly anxious over the outcome of the May-June general election after opinion polls on Monday showed an advance for either the left or the right.
On currency markets, the dollar steadied in Europe after overnight volatility but sterling stole the limelight, climbing almost two pfennigs and more than one cent after the interest rate rise.

"The market is looking more at the BOE independence measures than the rate rise and the forex market at least is taking the view that this will mean a tighter overall monetary policy than previously seen," said Peter Wood, trader at Bank of Boston.

The dollar meanwhile retreated from overnight highs against the mark and the yen amid some fresh optimism about economic activity in Germany and Japan but traders said there was little net change in the U.S. currency from Monday's levels.
The dollar was at 1.7290 marks by midday compared with 1.7286 late on Monday.

Details of the April German unemployment report leaked out on Monday and proved broadly in line with the official data released early Tuesday. Seasonally-adjusted jobless rose 8,000 during the month, with a drop in the unadjusted unemployment rate to 11.3 percent from 11.7 percent in March.
Earlier, the April German Purchasing Managers Index reinforced a view of a recovering German economy.
Jitters about an interest rate rise in Japan are more pronounced and the yen gained against both the dollar and mark overnight while Japanese government bond yields pushed higher.
STOCKS PRICES AT 1130 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 66.0 points at 4,521.6.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 17.06 points at 2,655.70.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 37.79 points at 3,566.57.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7290 marks compared with 1.7286 marks late in Europe on Monday. It was at 125.95 yen, compared to 126.62 on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $342.80 an ounce, compared to Friday's close in London of $340.05. Silver was $4.76.
